- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early or too high after sharp price spikes in history, then overshoot and fail to correct downward.
- Mean reversion is underappreciated — model fails to recognize that prices often revert to lower levels after recent highs.
- Model exhibits lagged response to recent price drops — underestimates downward momentum.
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward higher values, especially when history includes recent high prices.
- Model overreacts to short-term volatility — forecasts spike excessively after minor price movements.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 10 days of the 30d window, then gradually adjust — but often too late to capture true trend reversal.
- Model fails to account for seasonal or cyclical patterns — e.g., price dips in late Q4 or early Q1 are not sufficiently discounted.
